aliases: Ban Xieng Lek and Ban Xang Khong
hero.description: Ban Xang Khong is a short craft detour rather than a major excursion: just outside Luang Prabang, small workshops show mulberry-bark saa paper drying in the sun and traditional textile weaving in a village setting along the river.
steps: Come by bicycle, tuk-tuk or on foot
Watch weaving where workshops are active
Keep the visit light and informal
hero.rhythmNote: This works best as a one-hour extension of a slow day in town, not as a destination you need to build half a day around.
hero.photoNote: North of central Luang Prabang · along the river

chapters.label: THE CRAFT
chapters.title: Come to see how familiar Luang Prabang souvenirs begin
chapters.body: Ban Xang Khong and neighbouring Ban Xieng Lek are known for posa or saa paper made from mulberry bark and for handwoven textiles. The useful part of the visit is seeing those materials in process: paper sheets drying outside, fibres becoming decorative paper and looms turning thread into finished cloth.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: If you only want to buy a scarf, stay in town. Come here because seeing the making process matters to you.

items.label: Distance
items.detail: Close enough for a short tuk-tuk ride, bicycle outing or longer walk depending on the current river crossing.

items.label: Time
items.detail: Enough to see a few workshops without stretching a small craft village into a half-day attraction.

items.label: Cost
items.detail: The visit is built around village workshops and shops; purchases are entirely optional.

items.label: Best approach
items.detail: Go while workshops are active and there is enough light to see paper-making and weaving.

faq.question: What is Ban Xang Khong known for?
faq.answer: Mulberry-bark saa paper and traditional textile weaving are the main craft traditions visitors can see in the village area.

faq.question: How long should I spend there?
faq.answer: One to two hours including the short transfer from Luang Prabang is plenty for most visitors.

faq.question: Do I need to buy anything?
faq.answer: No. Shopping supports local workshops if you find something you genuinely want, but there is no obligation to purchase.

faq.question: How do I get there?
faq.answer: Official Luang Prabang tourism information places the villages about 3 km from town and lists tuk-tuk, bicycle and walking as possible approaches depending on the river crossing in use.

seo.title: Ban Xang Khong Weaving Village Guide | Atlas
seo.description: Visit Ban Xang Khong near Luang Prabang for a short look at saa-paper making, weaving workshops and a low-key craft village by the river.
